research_rationale: EO 5881 (July 9, 1932), read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original), is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 further exempting William L. Hill, John Lewis May and Leonard Magruder (Treasury) from compulsory retirement 'and continued in the service until August 1, 1932', to afford time to appoint successors. It follows the earlier exemption order of June 30, 1932 recited in its text (whose exemption ran to July 10, 1932; that order's number is not in the project's identity universe, so it is not cited by number here). The order ends by its own terms on 1932-08-01. NOTE: the machine TERM record's stated_end_date (1932-07-10) misreads the recital of the earlier order's term; its span (chars 910-1759 of the held text) contains the operative words 'until August 1, 1932', which govern. Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.
earlier_end_check: Own-terms expiry on the stated date. An individual employee's death or voluntary separation before that date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, a termination of the order; no held record shows any such event, and no later order amends, revokes or extends this order before the stated date (see search). The until-date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act. The recited July 10, 1932 date is the end of the earlier exemption of June 30, 1932, not of this order; this order's own term starts where that one stopped. Searches judged adequate for this narrow, short-lived exemption: the USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude any current-law reference, and the OFR catalog search (1937 onward, coverage warning) is supplemented by my own bounded search, on 2026-10-19, of the held WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, every numbered entry) and of all 526 held Hoover OFR 1974 compilation texts (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts) for each exempted person's surname. That search found the serial extension orders that do exist for other persons in this family (EO 6615 and EO 6974 for Jacob L. Nuber, EO 6975 for Charles J. James) but no later order naming the person(s) exempted by this order.
scope_check: Whole order is one clause covering three named persons with the same term; no partial amendment or revocation of any person's exemption is held or found.
savings_check: Read the order for savings or continuing effects: none stated; accrued service/pay only. Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term, and no later order names it.
